plays.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR (S&P 500 health care stocks)
plays.headline: Hide in the hospital: long health care
thesis: Rotation: after the hot CPI, money left tech (XLK -2.98%) for defensives. XLV rose 2.53% on 11.8M shares, 1.4x its 8.5M average.
Trend: closed at $173.96, above its 50-day ($169.41) and 200-day ($157.28) averages. RSI 52 leaves room before overbought.
Catalysts inside the 5-session window: ISRG reports Oct 20 after the close; TMO, ABT, DHR and ELV report Oct 21 before the open.
risks: PPI and retail sales land at 5:30 am PT Thursday and can flip the rate story before the open.
A tech rebound would pull money back out of defensives.
The 52-week high at $176.60 is resistance, and a stop does not protect against an overnight gap.
plays.dog: The dog lay down in front of the medicine cabinet and refused to move. In dog, that is a strong buy.

plays.name: Microsoft
plays.headline: Software over chips: long Microsoft
thesis: Rotation inside tech: software bounced while chips sank. ServiceNow +6.1%, Salesforce +4.6% and Adobe +4.6%, against semis (SMH) -1.0%. MSFT rose 1.08% to $539.44 on 23.6M shares vs a 20.8M average.
Trend: above its 20-day ($516.37), 50-day ($503.91) and 200-day ($434.78) averages, with higher closes from $490.30 on Sep 16. RSI 62 leaves room before overbought.
Room to the high: 2.6% under the 52-week high of $553.72. Analysts: 56 buy, 3 hold, 0 sell, mean target $593.20. Earnings are Oct 28, after the 5-session window.
risks: Wholesale inflation ran hot (PPI +6.3% a year) and the 10-year sits near 5.1%; a rate scare hits long-duration tech first.
The AI trade is wobbling: semis fell for a seventh straight session, and a spillover into AI software would hit MSFT.
The $553.72 52-week high is resistance, and a stop does not protect against an overnight gap.
plays.dog: The dog walked past the chip bowl, sat on the keyboard and opened a spreadsheet. In dog, that is a strong buy.

plays.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
plays.headline: Oil up, tech down: long energy at a 52-week high
thesis: Relative strength: on a day the S&P 500 fell 1.09% and tech dropped about 3%, XLE rose 2.52% to $68.24, a 52-week closing high, on 37.5M shares vs a 29.6M two-week average. Top holdings ExxonMobil (+2.46%) and Chevron (+2.59%) also hit 52-week highs.
Trend: above its 20-day ($63.72), 50-day ($63.33) and 200-day ($57.50) averages, up 11.0% from the $61.50 close on Sep 30 and 60% above the 52-week low of $42.64.

Catalyst and calendar: Brent tested $110 a barrel midday and USO rose 2.83%. The fund has no earnings and its next ex-dividend date is Dec 21; ExxonMobil and Chevron report Oct 30, after the 5-session window.
risks: The oil spike is headline-driven; a quick pullback in crude would hit XLE first.
Stretched: 7.1% above its 20-day average after an 11% run in 12 sessions. Breakouts on a red tape can fade fast.
A broad selloff can drag everything down, and a stop does not protect against an overnight gap.
plays.dog: The dog walked past the chip bowl again, lay down on the gas bill and refused to move. In dog, that is a strong buy.

plays.name: Amazon.com
plays.headline: Amazon's upgrade-day breakout: long AMZN
thesis: Catalyst with volume: AMZN rose 4.98% to $262.45 on Oct 19 after Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $350, on 54.8M shares vs a 34.5M two-week average, while the S&P 500 gained only 0.41%.

Breakout: the $262.45 close is the highest since Aug 28 and tops the $245.96-$262.43 closing range of the past seven weeks. It reclaimed the 20-day ($253.23) and 50-day ($257.08) averages and sits 8% above the 200-day ($242.73). Above the range, the stock traded $265-$284 in early August.
Calendar and consensus: no dividend, and earnings are Oct 29 after the close, after the 5-session window ends Oct 26. Analysts: 69 buy, 2 hold, 0 sell, mean target $332.96.
risks: Big-tech earnings land mid-hold: Tesla and Meta report Wednesday Oct 21 after the close, and a bad reaction can drag every megacap.
Upgrade pops often fade, and the stock stalled near $263-$264 twice this month (Oct 9 and Oct 12 highs of $262.80 and $263.70).
The tape is fearful: CNN Fear & Greed read 17.9 (extreme fear) and only 43% of S&P 500 members are above their 50-day average. A gap can skip the stop.
plays.dog: The dog dragged an empty delivery box to the front door and sat in it for an hour. In dog, that is a five-day strong buy.
